context:
Handle the three defects separately; they have different correct remedies.

DECISION GATE w1 (trust): decide per bundle-cohort, from provenance evidence, whether it is maintainer-run or a genuine outside submission. Relabel ONLY those with maintainer provenance. Do not bulk-flip the column. If provenance for a cohort cannot be established from results-data/README.md, the manifest sidecar, or the originating UAT run record, leave it community-submission and say so.

DECISION GATE w3 (no-query rows): choose ONE per cohort -- re-run to produce per-query timings, or withdraw the bundle from the public corpus. Do not leave undisplayable rows in a curated preview.

DECISION GATE w4 (validation): choose ONE per bundle -- re-run under validation so phases.validation.status becomes PASSED, or downgrade summary.validation to not_run so the site stops asserting a check that never happened. Never edit summary.validation upward to match a claim.

Then add a corpus admission check so all three classes fail closed on the next submission rather than being re-litigated.
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-23 against the built snapshot results-explorer/public/data/results.duckdb (207 rows) and the 207 bundles under results-data/bundles/ (203 flat + 4 nested under ssb/<platform>/sf*/).

Three independent defects make the public corpus far less useful than the data it already contains:

1. TRUST MISLABELLING (largest lever). is_ranking_eligible is FALSE for 192 of 207 rows. 191 of those carry ranking_exclusion_reason='trust_not_rankable' purely because trust_label='community-submission'. results-data/README.md:38-46 documents these bundles as the maintainer-run UAT sweep of 2026-05-02 -- they are not outside submissions. The leaderboard therefore renders 15 rows. Correcting the label on genuinely maintainer-run bundles takes it to ~206.

2. RESULTS WITH NO QUERY DATA. 60 of 207 rows have display_exclusion_reason='no_queries' and zero matching rows in query_executions (amplab 9, h2odb 9, tsbs_devops 9, tpch_skew 9, ssb 9, nyctaxi 9, coffeeshop 6). They cannot be displayed, compared, or ranked. They are corpus weight with no reader value.

3. VALIDATION CLAIMED BUT NOT RUN. 112 of 207 bundles report summary.validation = passed/partial while phases.validation.status = NOT_RUN (83 NOT_RUN+passed, 29 NOT_RUN+partial). The explorer surfaces validation_status='passed' for 142 rows. docs/development/result-integrity-validation.md:31-39 states not_run is not publication-clean. Publishing 'validated' numbers that were never validated is the fastest way to lose a benchmarking project's credibility.

A bundle produced by current develop does NOT have defect 3: an official TPC-DS SF1 DuckDB run on 2026-08-23 emitted phases.validation.status=PASSED and summary.validation=passed consistently. These are legacy artifacts of the May 2026 sweep, so re-running is a viable remedy, not only a code fix.

This item gates the public launch of benchbox.dev/results/.

---

## SUPERSEDED BY THE 2026-08-23 TRUST CUT — re-measure before acting (noted 2026-08-29)

Every measurement above is against a corpus that no longer exists. PRs #1939 (develop) and #1940 (published-results) withdrew all 130 bundles run before 2026-08-23, including the entire 2026-05-02 UAT sweep this item is about.

Re-measured against the post-cut snapshot built from the 9 surviving bundles:

  total rows                9
  ranking-eligible          8
  excluded: failed_queries  1   (tpcds SF10 Spark, one failed query)
  trust labels              9/9 maintainer-run, zero trust_not_rankable

Defect 1 (trust mislabelling) has no remaining instances: no surviving bundle has a sidecar, so none is labelled community-submission. Defects 2 and 3 likewise have no surviving instances.

This item looks closeable as overtaken by events rather than fixed on its merits. Confirm before closing: the underlying failure mode (sidecar presence alone implying community provenance) was addressed separately and is documented in results-data/README.md, but nothing here re-verifies that on new data. Future coverage restored under restore-corpus-coverage-after-20260823-trust-cut is where it would resurface.

anti_patterns.dont: Raise summary.validation to match a claim, or lower phases.validation.status to hide the mismatch
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD re-run under validation, or downgrade the summary to not_run
anti_patterns.why: both make the corpus assert something no run produced

anti_patterns.dont: UPDATE results SET trust_label='maintainer-run' across the corpus
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD relabel only cohorts with recorded maintainer provenance, per cohort, with the evidence cited
anti_patterns.why: it destroys the community/maintainer distinction the submission trust model depends on and would silently promote any real outside submission

preserves.behavior: Genuine community submissions keep trust_label=community-submission and are never silently promoted to maintainer-run
The published-results branch remains the corpus archive; changes reach it by the normal submission/validation path
bundle_sha256 integrity: a relabel must regenerate the inventory hash, never leave the recorded hash stale
